findings.text: §10 names "both state writers" as the store's `_write_state` (`reckon/_store.py:1717`) and the `reckon/serve.py` POST handler, and claims the meta "goes only when a write lands", but `_replace_plan_text` (`reckon/_store.py:2448`, called by `edit_plan`'s replacement path at `reckon/mcp_edit_plan.py:2050` and `:2060`) is a third version-advancing state write that calls `write_state` without the opt-in; reproduced at this head, `read_state` on a plan with declarations `{s1: done, s2: implementable}` and an authored meta of 0.9 returns `impl_source=declarations`, `impl=0.5`, and `write_state(text, state)` returns text still carrying `name="plan-impl" content="0.9"` — so a node implementing §10 exactly as written passes all four done-when cases while a content edit through `edit_plan` leaves the meta stale, which is precisely the condition §10 exists to remove
